---
title: "Server values and tables"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

For app authors who keep edited tables or other values on the server.
This guide assumes you already have a form tracker.

## Track an edited table on the server

DT and rhandsontable send edit events, not a complete saved table. Keep the
edited table in a reactiveVal and give that reactive to `values`. This DT
example belongs inside the app's server function; the UI needs
`DT::DTOutput("visits_table")` and Save and Discard action buttons.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
table_rv <- reactiveVal(data.frame(visit = 1:3, score = c(2, 4, 6)))
tracker <- unsaved_track(
  inputs = character(),
  values = list(Visits = table_rv),
  value_outputs = c(Visits = "visits_table"),
  on_save = function() {
    save_visits(table_rv())  # your app's storage function
    TRUE
  },
  on_discard = function() table_rv(tracker$baseline()$Visits)
)
output$visits_table <- DT::renderDT({
  DT::datatable(table_rv(), editable = TRUE, rownames = FALSE,
                selection = "none")
}, server = TRUE)
observeEvent(input$visits_table_cell_edit, {
  table_rv(DT::editData(table_rv(), input$visits_table_cell_edit,
                        rownames = FALSE))
})
observeEvent(input$save, tracker$save())
observeEvent(input$discard, tracker$discard())
```

The list names are the value ids and labels. They must be unique and must
not clash with input ids. Supply at least one input or value. A reactive
expression also works: its first available result becomes the baseline.
Data frames compare column by column, using the usual comparison rules;
`compare = list(Visits = identical)` selects an exact comparison.

Changed values appear in `is_dirty()`, `count()`, `changed()` and `diff()`,
and count towards the badge. For example, a change summary can read
"a table of 12 rows -> a table of 13 rows". `change` is display text; the
`saved` and `current` list columns hold the evidence. A custom comparator can
report "table changed" even when the cell scan finds no difference.
Input changes appear first in `diff()`, followed by server values in list
order. `value_outputs` is optional:
with it, the mapped output is outlined while the value is changed; without it,
the value has no marker. Use module-local output ids.

`mark_saved()` snapshots server values too. To supply saved data explicitly,
use `tracker$mark_saved(values = list(Visits = saved_table))`. The package
never sends these values to the browser, even on discard. The table widget
still renders the data that your app gives it. Restoring the reactiveVal is
the app's job: `discard()` calls `on_discard`, which reads `tracker$baseline()`
in the example. Without that callback, the edited server value stays dirty.

## Read the change list

Give inputs names to set labels, for example
`unsaved_track(c("Full name" = "name"))`. Empty names use the id.
`diff()` returns `name`, `label`, `change`, `saved` and `current`.
A clean tracker returns those columns with no rows.

For tables with the same column names and row count, `change` lists up to
three changed cells in row order, then the number of remaining changed cells.
Each cell has a row number, column name and saved/current text.
If the shape changes, the summary describes the old and new tables.
These are positional summaries, not a keyed cell audit log. The
[review demo](live-demo.html#lab-result-review) builds its own cell audit rows.

## Choose comparison rules

`compare = NULL` uses the default comparison. Numeric values use
`all.equal()` with relative tolerance `1e-8`, or absolute tolerance near zero.
For exact amounts or ids, use `compare = list(amount = identical)`.
A single comparison function applies to all tracked fields. A named list
applies functions by input or value id. Other fields use the default.
Each function takes saved and current values and returns one non-missing
logical: `TRUE` means equal.

`unsaved_compare_text()` trims outer whitespace and treats empty text as
NULL. Set `trim = FALSE` or `empty_is_null = FALSE` to turn either rule off.

```{r, eval = TRUE}
equal_text <- unsaved::unsaved_compare_text()
equal_text("Ada", " Ada ")
```

See [Saving](saving.html) for save callbacks and snapshot rules.
